why: An atomic tier 2 increment read through a live query stays exact when people cheer at once; a counter row read once and written back from the page loses concurrent cheers and never updates for anyone else.
Recounting every row on each change is exact and live; the page's counter loses cheers and goes stale.

One counter row incremented atomically and read through one live query is the platform's own way to keep a total; a one-row query used only as a change trigger, then every page rescanning the whole table, works around it.
